clue.text: Polite staff essential to the establishment

parts.note: civil means courteous or polite
servants are the staff of a household

explanation.surface: Courteous employees are what keeps any institution running.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The establishment' is the ruling order of the state, which its permanent officials keep going; 'Polite staff' reads as praise for helpful workers.
explanation.definitionFit: Government officials are the permanent machinery of the British state, which the Establishment depends on.

clue.text: Enter country by first of military aircraft with cross on exterior

indicators.note: on exterior says the word for cross wraps round the other pieces

parts.note: cross means angry, irate

indicators.note: first of picks only the opening letter of the word military

parts.note: a MiG is a Russian fighter aircraft

explanation.surface: An invasion force arrives by military jet carrying a cross on its fuselage.
explanation.walkthrough: IRATE (cross) is split open around M (first of 'military') and MIG.
explanation.definitionFit: To settle permanently in a foreign land is to come in from abroad as a new resident.

clue.text: Fill one mug initially out cambridge sportsman left out

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: initially takes just the opening letter of the word mug
left out says the letter for left is dropped from the sportsman

parts.note: a Blue is a sportsman who has represented Oxford or Cambridge University

explanation.surface: Someone tops up a mug while a university athlete sits on the sidelines.
explanation.walkthrough: A Cambridge BLUE is a student awarded colours for representing the university at sport; 'left out' removes L to leave BUE.
explanation.definitionFit: To imbue is to saturate or permeate something, filling it with a quality or liquid.

clue.text: Given support, seek election

explanation.surface: A candidate who has won backing decides to run for office.
explanation.definitionFit: A stand is a frame that holds something up; in British usage to stand is to run as a candidate.

clue.text: Able to be detached over blame, perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps says the letters could be arranged otherwise, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Something might come off, which is a question of who takes the blame.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges the letters of OVER and BLAME.
explanation.definitionFit: Something detachable can be taken off or away from where it is fixed.

clue.text: Bear north, going astray that's out of keeping

indicators.note: going astray says the letters wander off their proper course into a new order

explanation.surface: A bear wandering northward is behaving strangely for its kind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going astray' rearranges the letters of BEAR and NORTH; 'that's' links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something repugnant is wholly incompatible with, or contrary to, a principle.

clue.text: All the participants scored

parts.note: a musical direction in a score telling every performer in the ensemble to play together

explanation.definitionFit: In a written score, the Italian marking means all voices or instruments perform at once.

clue.text: In France a President upset drink on board, liable to be erratic

parts.note: un is French for a

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means the word for drink is turned upside down, read backwards

parts.note: cider is an alcoholic drink
a table is a board, as in board and lodging

explanation.surface: A French head of state knocks over his drink at the dinner table.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns CIDER into REDIC, which sits 'on' TABLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Behaviour that cannot be foreseen is erratic by nature.

clue.text: First stage leading to improvement of dirty habits?

definitions.text: First stage leading to improvement of dirty habits?

parts.words: First stage leading to improvement of dirty habits?
parts.note: habits read as clothes, as a nun's habit: soiled garments go first into a container before washing

explanation.definitionFit: Dirty clothing is tossed into this hamper before it is washed and cleaned.

clue.text: North American peninsula queen's abandoned for African country

indicators.note: abandoned says the queen is dropped from the peninsula's name

parts.note: Iberia is the peninsula holding Spain and Portugal
ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the Queen

explanation.surface: A North American leaves the Iberian peninsula, deserted by royalty, for Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: ER (Elizabeth Regina) is the crossword's queen; removing it from IBERIA leaves IBIA.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a nation in south-west Africa, bordering Angola and South Africa.

clue.text: Holy figure mother placed outside a hospital cash machine

indicators.note: placed outside says the word for mother goes round everything that follows

parts.note: ma is an informal word for mother
H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs
ATM, automated teller machine, is a cash machine

explanation.surface: A mother leaves a saintly figure outside a hospital cash machine.
explanation.walkthrough: MA wraps round A, H and ATM together.
explanation.definitionFit: The title, Sanskrit for great soul, is given to a revered sage, most famously Gandhi.

clue.text: Dissolute type good at heart? A scoundrel

indicators.note: at heart says the letter for good sits in the middle of the other word

parts.note: a roué is a debauched, dissolute man

explanation.surface: Is a debauched man really good underneath, or simply a villain?
explanation.walkthrough: G goes into the middle of ROUE.
explanation.definitionFit: A rogue is a dishonest rascal or villain.

clue.text: Consequence of road amusement

explanation.surface: Roadworks force a detour that turns into a pleasant outing.
explanation.definitionFit: Closing a road forces traffic onto an alternative route; separately, a pastime or entertainment is a distraction from routine.

clue.text: Board is effecting business transactions

parts.note: deal is a plank or board of pine or fir
is shortened to 's gives S

explanation.surface: The company board is busy completing commercial agreements.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Board' looks like a company's directors, but deal is timber, a pine plank.
explanation.definitionFit: Deals are commercial agreements or bargains struck between parties.

clue.text: Way to get American student immersed in small brook

indicators.note: immersed in says the American student is dipped inside the word for way

parts.note: a street is a way or road
L is for learner, a student driver

explanation.surface: To reach a little stream, an American student wades in.
explanation.walkthrough: AM and L (learner) go inside STREET.
explanation.definitionFit: A rivulet is a tiny stream, the diminutive -let marking its small size.

clue.text: Retrospective puzzle about green' type seeking to overthrow system

indicators.note: about says the reversed puzzle goes round the word for green
Retrospective means looking back, so the puzzle word is read backwards

parts.note: a rebus is a picture puzzle
vert is the heraldic word for green

explanation.surface: Reflecting on a puzzle about environmentalism, a radical plots to bring down the system.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retrospective' turns REBUS into SUBER, which goes 'about' VERT, heraldry's green.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who undermines or tries to topple an established order is a revolutionary saboteur.

clue.text: Provide information about subordinate's separation

indicators.note: about says the word for informing goes round the subordinate

parts.note: to sing is slang for informing to the police
under means subordinate or lower in rank

explanation.surface: An informer gives the police details about a junior's divorce.
explanation.walkthrough: SING (inform, as a criminal grassing to police) goes round UNDER.
explanation.definitionFit: Tearing apart or dividing two things is a parting.

clue.text: Fabricated a musical instrument, having missed last party

indicators.note: having missed last says the final letter of the instrument is dropped

parts.note: the trumpet is a brass musical instrument
the DUP, the Democratic Unionist Party, is a Northern Irish political party

explanation.surface: A musician who skipped the end-of-term party invents a cover story.
explanation.walkthrough: The DUP is the Democratic Unionist Party of Northern Ireland; TRUMPET loses its last letter to give TRUMPE.
explanation.definitionFit: A false charge invented to incriminate someone is concocted.

clue.text: Kick for which official permission's needed?

explanation.surface: A footballer wonders whether a booting of the ball needs the referee's say-so.
explanation.definitionFit: In football a defender's hoof upfield clears danger; it also means authorisation, as for take-off or security.

clue.text: Try to get lift in Northumberland

indicators.note: in says the answer sits inside the county's name

explanation.surface: A traveller attempts to hitch a ride in a northern English county.
explanation.walkthrough: Northumberland is a county in north-east England; 'in' points inside its name.
explanation.definitionFit: To hitch-hike is to beg a ride by holding out your digit at the roadside.

clue.text: Workers will ensure their survival

parts.note: workers read as worker insects: these creatures live by eating such insects

explanation.definitionFit: The animals feed on termites and worker insects of colonies, which are their food supply.

clue.text: Content of doctor's old trunk

indicators.note: Content of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Inside an elderly physician's travelling chest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trunk' suggests a storage chest; it is the body.
explanation.definitionFit: The trunk of a body is its central part without head or limbs.

clue.text: Sailing up river fishing smack primarily uses net

indicators.note: primarily takes the first letter of each of the five words

explanation.surface: Heading upstream, a fishing boat casts its net.
explanation.walkthrough: 'net' looks like a fishing net, but it is the internet.
explanation.definitionFit: To browse the internet is to ride its waves of pages.

clue.text: Musical instrument exercises (piano is out)

parts.note: p is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly

indicators.note: out says piano and is stand outside the word for exercises

parts.note: taken as written
PE is physical education, school exercises

explanation.surface: An instrument practises its exercises while the piano is away.
explanation.walkthrough: The bracket reads as the piano being absent, but P and IS go round PE.
explanation.definitionFit: Bagpipes, often just called by this short name, are a single wind instrument.

clue.text: Origin of snails in a little butter, a dish once thought exotic?

indicators.note: in says the first letter of snails goes inside the butter

parts.note: a pat is a small portion of butter

indicators.note: Origin of takes the opening letter of snails

explanation.surface: Escargots cooked in butter were once a foreign delicacy.
explanation.walkthrough: S (origin of 'snails') goes in PAT, then A.
explanation.definitionFit: Italian noodles such as spaghetti were once novel, foreign food in Britain.

clue.text: Source of potentially life-threatening air in Rhine valley

definitions.text: Source of potentially life-threatening air in Rhine valley

parts.words: Source of potentially life-threatening air in Rhine valley
parts.note: air read as a song: the legendary siren on a Rhine rock whose singing lured boatmen to their deaths

explanation.definitionFit: In German legend a maiden on a rock above the Rhine sang so sweetly that sailors were wrecked.

clue.text: Leader of union gripped by inordinate desire for rest

indicators.note: gripped by says the leader of union is held inside the other letters
inordinate means disorderly, so the letters are put out of order
Leader of takes the opening letter of the word union

explanation.surface: A trade union boss is seized by an excessive craving for a break.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inordinate' rearranges DESIRE into RESIDE, which grips U.
explanation.definitionFit: A residue is what remains, the remainder left over.

clue.text: Items featured by Phi lately (in a word)?

definitions.text: Items featured by Phi lately (in a word)?

parts.words: Items featured by Phi lately (in a word)?
parts.note: joining Phi and lately into one word gives the hobby of collecting stamps; Phi is also a fellow Independent setter

explanation.definitionFit: Philately is the collecting of adhesive stamps used to pay for mail.
